headline: Revenue keeps climbing but margins slip on soft demand
summary_short: Rollins' Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 7.9% y/y to $1,078.6M (organic +5.7%), but operating margin fell 110bp to 18.7% as residential demand softened, and net income grew just 1.7% y/y to $143.9M ($0.30 diluted EPS).
summary_long: Revenue rose 7.9% y/y to $1,078.6M (organic +5.7%), but growth was uneven: residential organic revenue grew just 3.6% as consumer-initiated lead volume softened, while commercial and relationship-based channels (home builders, door-to-door) stayed strong. Operating margin compressed 110bp y/y to 18.7% as the cost base was sized for stronger demand than materialized; net income rose only 1.7% y/y to $143.9M ($0.30 diluted EPS). Adjusted EBITDA margin fell 120bp y/y to 21.9%. Free cash flow was $166.1M, down 1.2% y/y, funding $116.8M of acquisitions, $20.5M of buybacks, and $88.1M of dividends. Cash fell to $109.1M and short-term debt rose to $215.9M on incremental borrowings; long-term debt held flat at $487.1M and equity was $1,429.6M.

drivers.explanation: Management says results fell short of expectations: consumer-lead-driven residential pest control softened (search, digital media, inbound calls), while relationship-based channels (home builders, door-to-door) delivered solid organic growth.
Organic growth of 5.7% was driven by relationship-based channels and commercial/termite services growing faster than consumer-lead-driven residential lines, per management commentary.
Growth was limited to 1.5% (margin -110bp to 18.7%) because the cost structure remained sized for a stronger demand environment than the softer lead volumes that materialized this quarter.
